National Identity Cards 
†*121. SHRI KRIPALPARMAR: Will t he Minister of HOME AFFAIRS 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether there is a state of uncertainty about the announcement 
made by the Government a few years back for issuing the National Identity 
Cards to all citizens in the country; 
(b) if so, the reasons therefor; 
(c) whether due to the non-issuance of  such National Identity Cards, 
Government are not in a position to arrest the persons who are living in India 
illegally; and

RAJYA SABHA [14 July, 2004] 
(d) if so, Government's reaction thereto9 
THE MINISTER OF HOME AFFAIRS (SHRI SHIVRAJ V. PATH): (a) 
No, Sir. A Pilot Project on Multipurpose National Identity Card (MNIC) 
scheme, which was initiated in the selected areas of 13 States and Union 
Territories in April, 2003. is under implementation and is expected to be 
completed by December 2004. 
(b) Does not arise in view of (a) above 
(c) and (d) There are standing inst ructions to the State Governments 
and Union Territory administrations to detect and deport persons staying 
in India illegally under the provisions of the Foreigners* Act. 1946 The 
implementation of Multipurpose National Identity Card scheme would further 
facilitate identification of illegally staying foreigners. 
Rapid Action Police Force 
*122. SHRI SHAHID SIDDIQUi Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that the Rapid Action Police Force (RAPF) 
was formed basically to deal with urban violence and communal violence; 
(b) if so, whether any analysis of RAPF being successful in achieving 
its objectives has been made, 
(c) what is the percentage of different religious Minorities in this 
force; and 
(d) the steps being taken to improve its working? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI SRIPRAKASH JAISWAL;. (a) and (b) The Rapid Action Force was 
raised to deal with the communal riots and riot like situations. The force 
carries out intern?! assessment periodi cally to assess its achievements

Effect of rise in coal prices 
302. SHRI V. NARAYANASAMY: Will the Minister of COAL AND 
MINES be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that the steep rise in coal prices has its 
cascading effect in prices of steel and power sector in the country; 
(b) if so, whether it is a fact that the beneficiary common man is 
severely affected by the rise in prices of prime grade coal; and 
(c) whether Government have receiv ed representation from the steel 
and power industry to reconsider the decision? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COALAND MINES 
(DR. DASARI NARAYANA RAO): (a) and (b) Power sector and steel sector 
are major consumers of coal. Any increase in price of coal leads to increase 
in their cost of generation/production. It is estimated that the recent increase 
in coal prices by CIL would have an impact of less than 6 paise on the 
cost of generation of 1 unit of elec tricity and presuming the average price 
of steel as Rs. 25,500/- per tonne, the impact on steel would be less than 2%. 
(c) No, Sir.

Assistance under NCCF for Andhra Pradesh 
334. SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA: Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government of Andhra Pradesh has requested for 
early release of case assistance and rice from the National Calamity 
Contingency Fund for the December, 2003 cyclone; and 
(b) if so, the action taken in this regard? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI S. REGHUPATHY): (a) and (b) As per the existing scheme for 
financing relief expenditure, the State Go vernments are primarily responsible 
for undertaking relief and rehabilitation measures in the areas affected by 
natural calamities. The Government of India supplements the efforts of the 
State Governments by providing financial and logistic support, where 
necessary. 
Assistance for relief and rehabilitation in the wake of natural calamities 
is provided under two Schemes. A Calamity Relief Fund (CRF) has been 
constituted for each State. The Govern ment of India c ontributes 75% of 
the corpus of the CRF. The State Governments contribute 25%. The State 
Governments are required to meet t he expenditure for providing immediate 
relief to the victims of natural calamities from the CRF. A Committee under 
Chairmanship of the Chief Secretary of the State has been authorized 
under the Scheme of CRF to decide on  all matters connected with the 
financing of the relief expenditure. 
Where funds available in the CRF do not prove to be sufficient for 
meeting the expenditure on relief and rehab ilitation, in case a calamity of 
severe nature, financial assistance is also provided to the States from the 
National Calamity Contingency Fund (NCCF) in accordance with the laid 
down procedure. 
The Government of Andhra Pradesh had submitted a memorandum 
seeking financial assistance from NCC F and foodgrains in the wake of 
cyclone in December, 2003. A Central Team was deputed by the Ministry 
of Home Affairs to assess the situ ation and requirement s of funds. The 
report of the Central Team was considered by the Inter-Ministerial Group 
(IMG). The request of the State Govern ment along with the report of the 
Central Team and recommendations of the IMG thereon was to be placed 
before the High Level Committee for co nsideration and approval. However, 
in the meantime the High Level Committe e was required to be re-constituted 
after the change of the Government at the Centre. The meeting of the 
55 

RAJYA SABHA [14 July, 2004] 
re-constituted Committee has now be en convened on 14th July, 2004 to 
consider the request of drought and flood/cyclone affected States including 
the State of Andhra Pradesh for cyclone of December, 2003. 
Meanwhile the State Government have informed that they have met 
the expenditure on relief operations in  the wake of cyclone of December, 
2003, out of the funds available in t he CRF. It may be stat ed that the State 
of Andhra Pradesh was allocated an amount of Rs. 229.28 crore in the 
CRF for the year 2003-04 consisting of  Rs. 171.96 crore as Central share 
and Rs. 57.32 crore as State's share.

367. SHRI DATTA MEGHE: Will the Minister of POWER be pleased 
to state: 
(a) the State-wise details of the number of unelectrified villages to 
be electrified in the country; 
91 

RAJYA SABHA [14 July, 2004] 
(b) whether at present a village is considered to be electrified even 
if one household in the village has access to power; 
(c) if so, the details thereof; 
(d) whether Government propose to redefine the term 'village 
electrification' to provide for wider coverage of village households; 
(e) if so, the details thereof; 
(f) whether the Government have drawn any schedule for rural 
electrification; and 
(g) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF POWER (SHRI P.M. SAYEED): (a) State-wise 
details of un-electrified villages are enclosed as Statement. (See below) 
(b) to (e) As per the old definition "a village will be deemed to be 
electrified if the electric ity is used in the inhabited locality, within the 
revenue boundary of the village, for any purpose whatsoever". 
A new definition has come into force w.e.f. 2004-05. According to 
the new definition. 
A village would be declared as electrified if 
(i) Basic infrastructure such as Distribution Transformer and 
distribution lines are provided in the inhabited locality as well as 
the Dalit Basti/hamlet where it ex ists, (for electrification through 
Non-Conventional Energy Sources a Distribution Transformer 
may not be necessary); 
 
(ii) Electricity is provided to pub lic places like Schools, Panchayat 
Office, Health Centres, Dispensarie s, Community centres etc.; and 
 
(iii) The number of households elec trified should be at least 10% of 
the total number of households in the village, 
(f) and (g) According to the National Common Minimum Programme 
household electrification is to be completed in five years. 
For achieving this target, the rural electrification strategy has been 
drawn up, which envisages: 
(i) Creation of Rural Electricity Distribution Backbone (REDB) of 
33/11 KV substations, with at least one such substation in each 
block appropriately networked and linked to the State 
transmission system, 
 
(ii) Creation of Village Electricity Infrastructure ( VEI) by providing 
Distribution Transformer(s) with at least one such transformer 
in every village. 
92

(iii) Rural Households Electrification of unelectrified households from 
village distribution transformer(s). 
 
(iv) Decentralized distributed gener ation system for such villages 
where grid connectivity is either no t feasible or not cost effective.

National Electricity Policy 
368. SHRI RAMA MUNI REDDY SIRIGIREDDY: Will the Minister 
of POWER be pleased to state: 
(a) by when Government propose to announce the National 
Electricity Policy and Rural Electricity Policy; 
(b) what are the salient features of the proposed policy; 
(c) whether Government is seriously thinking of giving free power 
to farmers as a norm in the policy; and 
(d) if not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF POWER (SHRI P. M. SAYEED) : (a) and (b) 
The Central Government is in consultation with the States formulating 
National Electricity Policy, National Policy on stand alone systems for 
rural areas and non-conventional energy system and National Policy on 
electrification and local distributions in rural areas as required under the 
electricity Act, 2003. 
(c) and (d) As per the provisions of the Electricity Act, 2003, the 
State Electricity Regulatory Commissions have the powers to fix tariff for 
sale of electricity to consumers including farmers. However, if the State 
Government requires the grant of any subsidy to any consumer or class 
of consumers in the tariff determined by the State electricity Regulatory 
Commissions (SERCs), the State Govern ment shall pay to the concerned 
utility/licensees the full amount requi red to compensate the grant of 
subsidy. 
The matter of providing subsidy in tariff to a class of consumers is 
a matter exclusively in the domain of the State Government and the Central 
Government has no role whatsoever, in this regard.

Mega status for four big power projects 
377. PROF. ALKA BALRAM KSHATRIYA: 
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY : 
Will the Minister of POWER be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Ministry has examined Mega status for four power 
sector projects; 
(b) if so, what are the States in wh ich these four projects will be set 
up and by what time final decision in this regard is likely to be taken; 
(c) whether under Mega power projects policy, import of capital 
equipment will be free of customs duty for these projects; and 
(d) what are other concessions that will be provided after providing 
Mega status to these big four power projects? 
THE MINISTER OF POWER (SHRI P.M. SAYEED): (a) Under the 
mega power policy announced in November, 1998, 19 power projects 
were identified as mega power projects which were eligible for the 
concessions available under the policy. The mega policy was subsequently 
amended and the concessions are now available to all inter-State projects 
107 

RAJYA SABHA [14 July, 2004] 
which fulfill the basic criteria of mi nimum capacity of 1000 MW for thermal 
and 500 MW for hydel projects subject to certification by the Ministry of 
Power of the required conditions having been met. Thereafter three more 
thermal power projects of the National Thermal Power Corporation 
(NTPC) have been certified by the Ministry of Power. 
(b) The three mega projects of NTPC referred to above fall in the 
States of Orissa, Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh. 
(c) Import of capital equipment is free of customs duty for any 
power generation project which meets the various conditions laid down 
under the mega power policy and is duly certified by the Ministry of Power. 
(d) In addition to the customs duty waiver, the mega power policy 
also provides for deemed export benefits as per the EXIM policy to 
domestic bidders for the mega power projects. It also provides for 
continuance of the income-tax holiday regime with the provision that the 
tax holiday period of 10 years can be cl aimed by a promoter in any block 
of 10 years, within the first 15 years.

Statement 
The extracts from the supplementary report of the steering group on

6. Debt Restructuring Scheme 
6.1 The international interest rates are very low at present. Whereas 
the cotton textile industry is faced with high cost of capital duty loans 
availed prior to introduction of Technology Upgradation Fund Scheme, 
which carried the then prevailing high rates of interest. In order to enable 
Indian textile industry to compete in the global market, Government of 
India should set up a reconstruction fund with the objective of reducing 
cost of capital of existing textile units in the organised sector. It is estimated 
that the total exposure of the FIs to the textile sector in the form of term 
loan is in the region of Rs. 16000 crores, of this amount 1/3 is unlikely to 
be revived and may not be eligible for assistance. Thus, the total debt 
exposure that needs to be addressed is estimated to be about Rs. 10,000 
crores.The efforts under the restructured scheme will be to bring down 
the ultimate rate of interest to borrowers to around 8%. The aim of the 
reconstruction will be to restructure industry's existing high cost loans 
tied up in the past. 
6.2 It is recommended that: 
 
• All existing secured loans, excess drawing of working capital 
(which would be converted into working capital term loan) would 
be eligible to be covered under the fund. 
• As part of restructuring exercise, Fls/banks would reduce rate 
of interest on their existing secured loans to a threshold level of 
12% per annum. If the existing rates are lower, they would be 
maintained at that level. 
• The rate of interest on working capital would be brought down 
to PLR. 
• The Fls/banks shall waive all penal interest, liquidated damages 
etc. 
• Over due interest would be funded and converted into "zero 
121 

RAJYA SABHA [14 July, 2004] 
coupon debentures" to be repaid after liquidating the restructured 
loans along with interest. 
• An incentive of maximum 4% would be extended on the rate of 
interest leading to the final intere st cost to the textile units on 
term borrowings at 8% per annum. 
• The textile units would pay interest at the rate of 8%. Interest 
incidence upto 4% would be compensated to Fls/banks out of 
the proposed fund. 
• The loans covered under TUFS and External Commercial 
Borrowings would not be eligible under the scheme. 
• The restructured loans alongwith 8% interest would be repaid in 
a maximum period of 10 years including 2 years moratorium. 
After 10 years period no interest incentive would be extended to 
any unit. 
 
6.3 The liabilities eligible for restructuring would include secured 
liabilities and excess working capital on the cut off date. 
6.4 The scheme would remain open for two year from the date of 
announcement. Loan given during these two year period shall not be 
eligible under the scheme. Any fresh loan for modernisation and expansion 
would be eligible for interest relief under TUFS. 
6.5 The initial size of the recons truction fund will be Rs. 500 crores. 
Additional requirement of fund could be assessed on the pace and 
success of the scheme.

IMPORTANCE 
Incidents of suicide by farmers in various parts of the country and remedial 
measures taken by Government with regard thereto 
SHRI S.S. AHLUWALIA (Jharkhand): Sir, I beg to call the attention 
of. the Minister of Agriculture on the incidents of suicide by farmers in 
various parts of the country, and remedial measures taken by the 
Government with regard thereto. 
THE MINISTER OF WATER RESOURCES (SHRI PRIYARANJAN  
DASMUNSI): Sir, the cases of suicide by farmers have been reported from 
the States of Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Orissa, Maharashtra, Punjab, 
Rajasthan and Tripura. The number of cases of suicide has been significant 
in Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Orissa and Maharashtra in the recent period 
as reported. However, the Government of Orissa has clarified that the 
cases of suicide by farmers in this State were not due to causes related to 
agriculture. The main causes as reported by the State Governments for 
committing suicide by farmers are crop failure, indebtedness, high rate of 
interest on loans, dro ught, social and economic  insecurity, incurable 
ailments, addiction to alcohol and family disputes. 
In order to tackle the problems of the farmers, the Common Minimum 
programme of the Government of UPA has identified areas requiring 
focussed and priority attention. Some of the important action points are, 
doubling rural credit in three years, easing the burden of debt, high interest 
rate and nursing cooperative banks to health, dry land farming, development 
of horticulture, improvement of water management and protection to farmers 
from imports and falling international prices. 
In order to achieve these objectives, the Finance Minister in his Budget 
Speech has announced a number of initiatives to provide relief to the 
farmers. Notable among them are, accelerating the completion of irrigation 
projects, investing in rural infrastructure, providing farm insurance and 
livestock insurance, improving agric ulture product markets and promoting 
agri-businesses and appointment of a Task Force on reforms in the 
cooperative banking system. 
ft is proposed to undertake restruct uring of debt of the farmers by 
the commercial banks, Regional Rural Banks and cooperatives. Debts 
of farmers in distress will be rescheduled /restructured in districts declared 
as calamity affected by the State Government with longer repayment 
period at current interest rates including an initial moratorium of two years. 
Farmers in arrears will receive the benefit of rescheduling of loans in 
143 

RAJYA SABHA [14 July, 2004] 
default to enable them to become eligible for fresh credit. The system of 
one-time settlement for defaulting small and marginal farmers will be put 
into operation. 
The Central Government has taken up various schemes and 
programmes for enhancing production of agriculture and horticulture crops 
like Macro-Management Scheme, Technology Mission on Horticulture in 
the North-East including Sikkim, Uttaranchal, Jammu and Kashmir, 
Integrated Scheme of Oilseeds, Pulses, Oil palm and Maize, Technology 
Mission on Cotton, Technology Mission on Coconut and On Farm Water 
Management in Eastern India. T he farmers are receiving financial 
assistance under different schemes. The Government has also provided 
safety nets in the form of National Agriculture Insurance Scheme (NAIS), 
Farmers Income Insurance Scheme (FIIS) against production loss and 
Minimum Support Price (MSP) and Market Intervention Scheme (MIS) 
against decline in prices. 
The drought relief assistance is given to the States both in the form 
of financial assistance and foodgrains as and when necessary. 
[THE VICE-CHAIRMAN (SHRI DINESH TRIVEDI) in the Chair] 
Since August, 2003, Andhra Pradesh has received Rs. 140.86 crores 
and 7.2 lakh MTs of foodgrains, Kar nataka Rs. 332.15 crores and 7.29 
lakh MTs of foodgrains and Kerala Rs. 30.65 crores and 0.61 lakh MTs of 
foodgrains. 
State Governments also provide re lief to the affected families. 
Government of Andhra Pradesh have decided to provided financial 
assistance, i.e., an ex gratia of Rs. 1 lakh to the family/next of kin of the 
deceased farmers as economic support besides loan settlement up to a 
ceiling of Rs. 50,000 as one-time settlement to creditors, each family is 
given a house under Indira Awas Yojana, admission to wards in Social 
Welfare Residential Schools Hostels.  In Karnataka, compensation of 
Rs. 110.22 lakhs to affected families of the farmers has been given. The 
interest on short-term loan has been waived and a rebate of 5.5 per cent 
is allowed on medium-term loan. Furthe r, fertilizers and seeds are supplied 
at subsidised rates. In Maharashtra, the heirs of the deceased were given 
assistance of Rs. 1 lakh from the Chief Minister's Relief Fund. 
The Government is fully conscious of the hardships of the farmers 
and will spare no efforts to solve their problems. Thank You.

DR. VIJAY MALLYA (Karnataka): Sir, I will not exceed my time. 
Thank you. Sir, the problem of farmer suicides which I have been a painful 
witness to can be summarised as being a problem with middlemen. There 
are several agricultural credit institut ions all over Indi a. Whether the kind 
of finance is actually available to the poor farmers at rates of interest and 
on terms that are intended by the Go vernment is something that needs 
serious examination. There is a breed called loan sharks or middlemen 
who conveniently ensure that the poor farmer cannot directly borrow from 
the credit institutions, that the middlem en, in fact, facilitate the loan and 
charge the poor farmer exorbitant rates of interest which he simply cannot 
afford. I have examined this. The middlemen also make the farmer who is 
most of the time illiterate, sign pieces  of paper pledging their land holdings 
and when they are unable to pay, they come down on them and harass 
them to an extent which really drives them to suicide. Something needs to 
be done urgently to eradicate these middlemen. The other point that I 
would like to make about middlemen is in the value chain. If one would 
care to examine the price that the farmer gets for his produce and the 
price at which the very same produce is  sold to the end consumer, you will 
notice, Sir, that there are several middlemen along the way, which means 
that the poor farmer gets the least realisation for what he produces. This is 
another aspect that needs immediate Gove rnment attention. Finally, Sir, 
we announced many schemes for the benefit of the farmer but there is no 
accountability in ensuring that the farmers actually benefits from these 
schemes, in the way which are intended. Thank you.

employment. The Banks of Kerala have already expressed their anxiety.

Need to Include the State of Andhra Pradesh in National 
Drainage Technology Programme 
SHRIMATI VANGA GEETHA (Andhra Pradesh): Sir, the State of 
Andhra Pradesh has got the oldest delta s. The soils being heavy in these 
areas, the State is facing severe problem of water logging and impeded 
drainage. An estimated area of about 1.1 m hectare suffers from drainage 
congestion and water logging, a large part of which lies in the Krishna 
Godavari delta. Out of this, the yiel d loss is hundred per cent in about 0.2 
m hectare, fifty per cent in 0.3 m hectare, and, about twenty five per cent 
in 0.2 m hectare in the Krishna Godavari delta. Also a chain of fish ponds 
have sprung up in the coastal area, converting fertile rice fields (about 
50,000 hectare) for this purpose obstructing free flow of drainage water 
during times of heavy rains and floods. This has added new dimension to 
the chronic problem of drainage in t he coast. The State of Andhra Pradesh 
is one of the prosperous agricultural States of India, significantly contributing 
to the production of foodgrains, oilseeds and commercial crops. The 
production and productivity of crops will be further enhanced in this State 
if due attention is paid to the drai nage improvement. It is understood that 
the State has not been included in the National Drainage Technology 
Programme, contemplated by the Union Government. 
The Government of India has been requested to include the State of 
Andhra Pradesh in the National Drainage Technology Programme for under- 
taking research as well as for trials, demonstrations for large scale adoption 
of drainage improvement measures in the common areas of the State.

Need to Legislate to Protect the Lower Riparian States 
SHRI T.T.V. DHINAKARAN (Tamil Nadu): Sir, I wish to impress upon 
the need for bringing a suitable legislation as envisaged in Entry 56 of the 
Union List given in the Constitution, to protect the interests of lower riparian 
States. The inter-State river water di sputes adjudication under the Inter- 
State Water Disputes Act of 1956, does  not provide timely help to the 
suffering States. The Cauvery water dispute is a glaring example. The 
Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal was set up in June, 1990, and an interim 
award was given on 25th June, 1991. Af ter persistent effort by the hon. 
Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, the interim award was gazetted by the Union 
Government on 11th December, 1991. Ev en that did not bring solace to 
Tamil Nadu. After 14 years of anxious wait, justice is still not in sight. 
Same is the fate of all the riparian States of 14 major and 9 medium inter- 
State rivers. Anticipating such situ ations, our constitution-makers have 
provided ample power to the Union under Entry 56 of List 1 to legislate for 
the regulation and development of inter-State rivers and river valleys. Time 
has come for the Centre to act in this direction. Such a step by the Union 
will have the advantage of ensuring a quick solution to such disputes. This 
will also take care of the voices of dissent raised against the linking of 
major rivers in the country. So, I appeal to the Government to bring a 
comprehensive legislation under Entry 56 of List 1 and safeguard the 
interests of lower riparian States.

Anandamargi sanyasis and one sanyasin were burnt alive by a mob on 
the Bijan Setu (Ballygunj Railway Overbridge) in broad daylight. The case

over to the CBI since the West Bengal police is working under political 
pressure. The State Government should compensate the family of Dolui 
and other victims of arson.

Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh or even West Bengal, are dying of starvation.

called, Amlasol in Midnapore. This area comes under a village called 
Belpahari where people are reportedly dying of starvation and malnutrition.

a letter to the hon. Chief Minister of West Bengal narrating the tragedy of

district in Tamil Nadu, it has no ma jor industry. Two years ago, a full- 
fledged radio station was set up at Dharmapuri. The radio station was 
constructed at a cost of  Rs. 4.03 crores. All the infrastructural facilities 
have been completed and the station is ready for operations. 
At present, the statio n has a 3 KW capacity and can be heard up to 
40 Kms. distance. However, the stat ion has the capacity and potential to 
function with 10 KW which can be heard beyond a distance of 60 Kms. 
The station has an independent studio and other facilities required for a 
separate station. However, the ra dio station has not commenced its 
operations. It is understood that the necessary staff have not been provided 
and that is why it has not commenc ed its operations. I demand that 
necessary staff should be posted immediately so that the radio station 
commences its operations. Otherwise, all the money and labour would 
become a waste.

is being set up at Dharmapuri. However, the work is progressing at a slow 
pace. I demand that the work should be completed on a top priority by 
allocating adequate funds. Moreover, ev en smaller districts have FM radio 
stations. Dharmapuri is a large district and if an FM channel is provided,

Need to Exempt Customs Duty on Raw Material Imported for 
Manufacture of Micro Irrigation System in Andhra Pradesh 
SHRI RAMA MUNI REDDI SIRIGIREDDY (ANDHRA PRADESH): 
Sir, the State of A ndhra Pradesh is the "Rice Bowl " of the country, but it is 
facing acute shortage of water over the last three to four years and this is 
severely hampering the agricultural acti vity in the State. In Andhra Pradesh 
State, agriculture contributes 30 per  cent to the State's GSDP. The 
sustainability of this vital economic ac tivity for 60 per cent of the State 
population is severely undermined due to the dwindling of groundwater 
resources and misuse of surface water. The Government of Andhra Pradesh 
is planning to launch a Micro Irrigation Project to achieve sustainable 
growth in agriculture and for an effective management of water, with a 
project outlay of Rs. 1,200 crores, cove ring an area of 2.5 lakh hectares in 
two years. The aim of the project is to take the benefits of micro irrigation 
to the agricultural field of every farmer in Andhra Pradesh. The Government 
of Andhra Pradesh is giving a subsidy of  50 per cent on every micro irrigation 
unit to every eligible farmer. In spite of this subsidy, the Micro Irrigation 
Systems are fairly capital-intensive. 
So, to reduce the cost of micro irrigation equipment, the Government of 
Andhra Pradesh has already exempted Sales Tax and the Union Govemment 
too has exempted the Central Excise Duty. But, to make the equipment more 
affordable to the farmer, I request the Fi nance Minister to exempt the Customs 
Duty to be levied on raw material that is used in the production of Micro 
Irrigation System. The exemption would bring down the pric e of the equipment 
by 50 per cent which helps the farmer in getting higher crop. 
Matter Raised with Permission—contd.
